answeredFailures: Failure 1 (blocking): the note's Evidence said `du` reports 0 blocks for such a file on this gVisor overlay, so `df` is the instrument and `du` is not. Measured false. Fixed at 76e516e3e34bd0c584ac4bf719963d0203da116c: the note now says `du` pointed at a path reports the file normally, that the blind instrument is the one-filesystem walk `du -x` (a written file reports a different device from its parent on this overlay, so `du -x` skips it), and names what a reader should run — `du -sh ~/.cache` without `-x` for a directory, `df -k --output=used /` for the whole container filesystem — and what to avoid, `du -x` and `df -x`.

Failure 2: the not-charged list called all five of /home/legion/.config, /var/run/legion/private, /var/run/legion/state, /var/run/legion/launcher and /var/run/legion/gh 'in-memory directories'. Fixed: the three emptyDirs are named as in-memory emptyDirs mounting tmpfs rw, and /var/run/legion/launcher and /var/run/legion/gh as read-only credential mounts (Secret volumes, 9p ro) a reader cannot write to at all. Their not-charged verdict is unchanged, which is what the tester found too.
Failure 3: 'A habit of "put the big download in /tmp" is evicted for here' was ungrammatical. Fixed: 'gets the pod evicted here'; the rest of the sentence is byte-identical.

No permanent test was added, as the tester and the architect both judged: a grep over prose is a source-text test this repository's conventions forbid, the repository has no checker over docs/solutions/, and each finding's re-runnable command is the evidence.

proof.criterion: Failure 1's correction is the measured one: `du` sees these files and `du -x` does not, so the note names the instrument a reader should actually use.
proof.surface: A live Legion role container — this issue's own implementer container in its Agent Sandbox pod — independently of the tester's container, which measured the same thing on its own overlay.
proof.command: dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/probe bs=1M count=200; stat -c 'blocks=%b dev=%d' /tmp/probe; stat -c 'dev=%d' /tmp; du -sk /tmp/probe; du -sk /tmp; du -sx -k /; du -x -a -d1 -k / | grep -w /tmp; mkdir -p /home/legion/.cache/probe && dd if=/dev/zero of=/home/legion/.cache/probe/f bs=1M count=200; stat -c 'dev=%d' /home/legion/.cache /home/legion/.cache/probe/f; du -sx -k /home; du -sh /home/legion/.cache
proof.observed: stat prints blocks=409600 dev=112 for the file against dev=114 for its parent /tmp; du -sk /tmp/probe prints 204800 and du -sk /tmp prints 217364, so du pointed at the path sees the whole file. du -sx -k / stays 42348 across the write and du -x -a -d1 -k / prints 0 for /tmp. The same holds from the home directory: the file written under /home/legion/.cache reports dev=112 against the directory's dev=114, du -sx -k /home stays 13516 with 200 MiB sitting there, while du -sh /home/legion/.cache reports 212M. These are the figures the note now carries, and they reproduce the tester's reading in a second container.
proof.negativeControl: The old sentence's own prediction is the control: if `du` really reported 0 blocks for such a file, `du -sk /tmp/probe` would print 0 and `du -sh ~/.cache` would be useless — it prints 204800 and 212M instead. The instrument that does read 0 is `du -x` (`du -x -a -d1 -k /` prints 0 for /tmp), which is exactly the distinction the corrected text makes, so the measurement separates the two rather than confirming either by itself.

trickyParts: The false claim had a true-looking source: `du -sx /` really does report no change for a 200 MiB write, which is how it was written in round 1. The device mismatch between a written file (dev=112 here, 143 in the tester's container) and its parent directory (114 / 145) is the whole mechanism, and it is only visible if you stat both. Any later measurement of this filesystem should stat the file as well as the directory before concluding anything about an instrument.

The round-1 PR body carried the same false parenthetical in its `E2E (implementer)` line. Because this repository squashes, the body becomes main's commit message, so the wrong claim would have entered history even though the note was fixed; the body was corrected in the same round.
